newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama grants asylum to Ecuador's deposed Bucaram.
newsitem.headline: Panama grants asylum to Ecuador's deposed Bucaram.

text.p: Ecuador's deposed President Abdala Bucaram has been granted political asylum in Panama, the Foreign Ministry said on Monday.
"The government of Panama has given political asylum to Bucaram, his wife, children and brother, effective last Thursday," spokesman Erich Rodriguez said.

The measure covered Bucaram's wife, Rosa Maria Pulley, their four children Jacobo, 18, Linda, 17, Abdala, 15, and Michelle, 13, and Bucaram's brother, Santiago, who was expelled from Ecuador's Congress.

Bucaram, who continues to call himself president, told a news conference on Monday he will meet Foreign Minister Ricardo Arias on Tuesday "to find out what my limits are since he confirmed that I have been granted asylum."
Speaking from his apartment in the Punta Paitilla district in Panama City, his wife and children at his side, Bucaram denied he was "throwing in the towel" by asking for asylum.

"How could I be throwing in the towel when my party is the largest in the country," he said. "I feel more powerful than ever. My soldiers are in Ecuador. I guarantee you that in Ecuador, there is no other leader," he said.
Bucaram was deposed by Congress on Feb. 6 on grounds of "mental incompetence" after only six months in office. He travelled to Panama a few days later.

The populist leader, known as "el loco" (the crazy one) for his eccentric personal style, lived in exile in Panama from 1985-90 after fleeing charges of corruption as mayor of his home city, Guayaquil.

News that Bucaram's asylum request was granted coincided with a peaceful protest staged by a small group of Ecuador's Embassy in Panama City. "We are against Panama giving Bucaram asylum," Emma Ortega, leader of a group of seven people, said.
She said they flew in from Ecuador on Monday to stage the protest. "Bucaram is an assassin," she told reporters without giving details about her group.

Ecuador's Supreme Court has issued a warrant for Bucaram's arrest on grounds of misuse of presidential funds. Congress has expelled 13 deputies, including his brother, who was accused of siphoning funds from the national budget.
